title: SignalPolarity::AutoDetect skewness heuristic resolves to the wrong (intensity-phase) polarity
baseline_evidence: n/a (new code path introduced by remediation)
current_behavior: compute_should_flip (src/rppg/signal.rs:558-581) flips when sample skewness > 0.3. BVP-phase (systolic-peak-positive) waveforms are positively skewed (SCAMPS d_ppg raw skew +0.42..+1.28, mean +0.72), so the heuristic flips signals that ALREADY satisfy the section 2.4 contract and keeps negatively-skewed intensity-phase signals unflipped. On 10 SCAMPS videos x 3 algorithms, auto polarity_resolved agrees with the d_ppg-correlation-maximizing choice in only 1/30 cases (green 10/10 wrongly 'normal' corr=-0.921; pos 10/10 wrongly 'normal' corr=-0.823; chrom 7/10 wrongly 'inverted' corr +0.362->-0.432, 3/10 'normal' of which 1 correct). Consistency per algorithm: green/pos consistent-but-wrong (10/10 normal); chrom inconsistent (7 inverted, 3 normal). Downstream harm if auto is trusted: chrom peak F1 0.768->0.723, chrom HR MAE 11.82->14.16 bpm vs correct phase.
notes: Silent wrong-polarity output labeled as contract-compliant BVP; no error raised. Fix direction: flip when skew < -0.3 (negative skew = intensity phase), or validate against Elgendi peak prominence asymmetry.
